name: Fire Party
label: Dischord
lede: Four friends out of a Revolution Summer basement, two EPs on Dischord, three months in Europe watching Dave Grohl drum for Scream, and a band that spent its whole life refusing the 'all-girl' tag.

eras.title: A basement, a fireplace, a name
eras.text: By the late 1980s, Dischord says, D.C.'s underground had produced dozens of bands but only a handful of the musicians in them were women. Fire Party came out of the tight circle around Revolution Summer, and one of its members had helped name that summer in the first place.

years.p: Amy Pickering, who worked at Dischord, and Chris Thomson coin "Revolution Summer" as an inside joke at a D.C. summer-jobs office. It ends up naming a whole season of D.C. bands.

q: It was a fire party and it solidified our bonds.
years.h: Fire Party forms in Natalie Avery's parents' basement
years.p: [[Amy Pickering|7898585a-f3dd-4ca3-bd20-777eaef63764]] sings, Natalie Avery plays guitar, Kate Samworth bass and [[Nicky Thomas|4fcca973-445f-41c3-952b-df7fa008777f]] drums, practicing in Avery's parents' basement. The name comes from a night the four stayed up until morning talking and laughing by a fireplace.
years.xp:
Natalie Avery has said, as quoted by Wikipedia, that the band grew out of a tight-knit group of people shaped by a very small music scene. Avery worked at Yesterday and Today Records, and Nicky Thomas and Kate Samworth worked at Olsson's Books and Records. Pickering, Avery and Samworth already knew each other.

Thomas had played in Lebensluste and In Pieces. She came to drums almost by accident, after junior-high band on flute, bassoon and percussion.

eras.title: Dedicated to Toni
eras.text: Fire Party's first year put it on stage at two landmark D.C. nights: its own debut, played in memory of a pioneer, and the first-ever Fugazi show seven months later.

years.h: Fire Party's first show, at d.c. space, is dedicated to Toni Young
years.p: Fire Party dedicates its debut set to Toni Young, bassist in Red C and later Dove, who Dischord says had recently died of pneumonia.
years.xp: Dischord's Red C history notes that a second Red C demo may have existed, but the tapes disappeared after Toni Young died.

years.h: Fire Party plays Fugazi's first show at the Wilson Center
years.p: A $5 benefit at D.C.'s Wilson Center for Dischord's State of the Union compilation. Fire Party shares the bill with [[Marginal Man|fff14e91-ae03-4105-8fbb-3a318d6c01ca]], Ignition and a brand-new band called [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]].

eras.title: Two EPs and three months with Scream
eras.text: Two records with Ian MacKaye at Inner Ear, and a long European run with Scream that drummer Nicky Thomas says changed her as a drummer. At home Fire Party kept getting sold as a novelty. In Europe, Dischord says, people listened.

years.p: The first 12-inch, recorded at Inner Ear and produced by [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]]. It opens with Jerk and Basis.

years.big: Judge the band, not the lineup.
q: really hated being thought of as an 'all-girl band'
years.h: Fire Party refuses the 'all-girl band' tag
years.p: Dischord says Fire Party tried to avoid the 'all-girl band' label being handed out, and found the novelty angle hard to escape, especially in the States.
years.xp:
Drummer Nicky Thomas told No Echo there were many attempts to treat them as a novelty, and they always resisted the role, downplaying it as much as they could.

Europe was different. Dischord's history says audiences there seemed more interested in the music being played than in who was playing it.

years.h: Fire Party appears on Dischord's State of the Union
years.p: The benefit compilation that Fugazi's first show at the Wilson Center raised money for finally comes out, with Fire Party on it.

years.cap: Scream and Fire Party on tour in Europe, 1989
years.h: Three months in Europe with Scream, watching Dave Grohl every night
years.p: Fire Party tours Europe with [[Scream|b9f52132-28af-4cea-9558-165cd125f9b7]], whose drummer is a young [[Dave Grohl|4d5f891d-9bce-45ae-ad86-912dd27252fa]]. Nicky Thomas told No Echo that three months of watching Grohl made her a completely different drummer.
years.xp: Wikipedia says Fire Party also supported That Petrol Emotion on the trip, and played Midwest shows with Scream. Nicky Thomas describes the European run as the thing that put the band's growth on overdrive.

years.h: Fire Party records a John Peel Session in London
years.p: During the Scream tour, Fire Party records a session for John Peel's BBC Radio 1 show: Basis, Are You On?, How To and Stray Bullet.
Fire Party's second 12-inch, back at Inner Ear, produced by Ian MacKaye and [[Ted Niceley|fbe203ef-a327-4d7e-af16-a10d55b7347d]]. It includes Pilate, Gethsemane, Only Nine Mottos and the title track.

years.h: Fire Party breaks up, without a blowup
years.p: Dischord dates the end of Fire Party to spring 1990. Drummer Nicky Thomas told No Echo the band simply ran its course after three or four years, as the members' lives changed.

eras.title: Nineteen songs, and what came after
eras.text: Dischord gathered both Fire Party EPs and the John Peel Session onto one CD, 19 Songs. The members went on to art, writing and other bands.

years.p: Both Fire Party 12-inch EPs, Fire Party and New Orleans Opera, plus the 1989 John Peel Session on one CD. The Peel version of Basis sits next to the original.

years.h: Kate Samworth turns to art; Nicky Thomas keeps drumming
years.p: Per No Echo, bassist Kate Samworth becomes an accomplished visual artist. Drummer Nicky Thomas keeps playing, with Hard Left, and is writing a memoir about being Black and punk in America.

years.h: Fire Party on the 20 Years of Dischord box set
years.p: Fire Party gets its place on the label's 2002 anniversary box set.

sources.title: No Echo: Past Forward #2, Fire Party
